Sponsors 🏅️

Access Awareness: Updates That Matter ♿️

We Are Pregnant! | Squirmy and Grubs | YouTube.com | September 8, 2026

Announcing their pregnancy, Shane and Hannah Burcaw share the news of a major new chapter for their family. The pair also partners with Babylist to help expecting families by purchasing items from selected registries shared by their community.

This Week’s Featured Advertisement ️

Can You Lead Without Bias? Try It — At The Next NW Diversity Learning Series Workshop September 23, 2026 | Save Your Spot! | Institute for Sustainable Diversity & Inclusion (ISDI)

Every organization says it wants creativity and innovation. Both require the same raw material — people who see what the group is missing, and who are free enough to say it out loud.

Bias taxes that freedom, and it’s costly. Bias rarely arrives as hostility. It arrives as a standard applied unevenly, a hire decided on fit, or an idea that lands differently depending on who says it.

Join this NW Diversity Learning Series workshop to learn how to:

  • Define competency checking; identify where it enters everyday leadership decisions — hiring, assignments, feedback, credit, and airtime.
  • Explain to a peer how biased decision patterns suppress creativity and innovation on a team.
  • Analyze one decision or process you personally own using an Applied Equity lens, naming the criteria in use and who those criteria advantage.
  • Use at least one non-shaming move to interrupt bias in a live conversation.

Register today!

Wednesday, September 23, 2026
9AM to 11AM Pacific
Virtual on Zoom

News 📰️

👉 Submit a news article for free here, with timing and placement determined by our editors.

👉 Submit a Sponsored News Article here, with timing and placement determined by you.

1.) Top 5 Most Clicked News Articles From Last Week 📊️

A.) Do I Actually Know What Animals Look Like?? | Molly Burke | YouTube.com | September 1, 2026

Reflecting on how blindness shapes visual understanding, Molly Burke considers what she knows about the appearance of animals. The conversation examines the gap between learned descriptions, touch, sound, and the mental images people form of the natural world.

B.) Recording: Official Launch of The Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion | Dr. Kirk Adams, Executive Director, ISDI | September 7, 2026

Here, Dr. Kirk Adams shares the full recording of the September 1, 2026 public launch of the Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion, the national membership community created by the Institute for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion to help people working in diversity, equity, inclusion, accessibility and belonging move from reactive, isolated survival mode to strategic, sustainable, collective power.

C.) Impending Changes to Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act | Nod.org | September 1, 2026

The U.S. Department of Labor’s final Section 503 rule, effective September 21, 2026, eliminates the CC-305 disability self-identification form, the 7% utilization goal, and required disability data collection for applicants, referrals, and hires. Nondiscrimination, affirmative action, reasonable-accommodation, and outreach requirements remain, while the contract coverage threshold rises to $20,000.

D.) The Doors Are Open: How to Join the Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion | Dr. Kirk Adams, Executive Director, ISDI | September 7, 2026

Here, Dr. Kirk Adams announces that the Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion went live on September 1, 2026, opened not with a webinar or a panel but with an “Ask Us Anything” hour of questions, frustrations, ideas and lived experience. He explains what the Coalition actually is: a way for members to move from reactive, isolated survival mode to strategic, sustainable, collective power, built on four words, Connect, Learn, Act, Together. He is direct about who it is for, which is everybody, and equally direct that disability inclusion and accessibility are not a side room in it but a dedicated space by design. Inside, he describes three things above all others: BELONG, the peer circles where saying “I am overwhelmed” is met with practical help rather than judgment; CLARITY, a trusted translation layer of plain-language briefings and expert-guided sessions; and POWER, the shared tools, cross-sector strategy and coalition-backed influence that turn isolated effort into coordinated action. In practice that means Ask the Experts office hours, a Member Lounge and Directory, a growing Resource Library, a Rapid Response Hub for the moments that will not wait, legislative and legal updates, podcasts featuring DEIAB voices, and a shared calendar of events worth your time.

E.) Hannah Was Almost Attacked Not Kidding | Squirmy and Grubs | YouTube.com | August 31, 2026

Recounting a disturbing encounter at a local park, Hannah and Shane Burcaw describe how a stranger’s unusual behavior escalated an ordinary outing into a frightening moment. The pair also use a dramatic reenactment to convey the tension of the incident and its aftermath.

September 14, 2026 📅️

2.) When Disclosure Costs You the Interview: Seattle’s Disability:IN Chapter Takes on the Question | DrKirkAdams.com | September 14, 2026

Here, Dr. Kirk Adams tells the story of the impossible choice that shaped his career. In 1983, fresh out of Whitman College with a degree in economics, he could either say nothing about his blindness and watch an interview collapse the moment he walked in with a long white cane, or disclose it at the top of his cover letter and stop getting phone interviews altogether. Two bad options, and no third one on offer. He connects that experience directly to “The Courage to Be Human at Work: Vulnerability, Access, and Connection,” a free 90-minute webinar hosted by Disability:IN Washington on Wednesday, September 30, 2026, and led by Linea Johnson, Founder and CEO of The Thrive Shift. Its central question, he writes, is one he recognized on sight: how do we create workplaces where people don’t have to choose between protecting themselves and belonging?

3.) Another Door to Knock On: Jennifer Bazer and the Palmetto Council of the Blind | DrKirkAdams.com | September 14, 2026

Here, Dr. Kirk Adams introduces Jennifer Bazer, President of the Palmetto Council of the Blind of South Carolina and a newly elected member of the Board of Directors of the American Council of the Blind, and makes the case for supporting the Council’s Kicking for a Cause online auction, which closes on September 20, 2026. Blind since birth, a social worker by training and a veteran of more than a decade managing large federal workforce programs, Bazer founded the Palmetto Council in 2023 with a deliberately simple aim: to give a newly blind South Carolinian, a family member who does not know where to turn, or anyone looking for a way in “another door they could knock on.”

4.) What We Inherit — and What We Must Build Next | By Dr. Kirk Adams, Executive Director, ISDI | DrKirkAdams.com | September 14, 2026

Here, Dr. Kirk Adams reflects on launching the Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion on September 1, in a span of days that also brought the deaths of Dolly Parton, Wendell Berry, and Gloria Steinem. He writes candidly about his discomfort at honoring three white figures in a piece about a coalition devoted to diversity, equity, inclusion, accessibility, and belonging, and he insists that the long struggle for freedom has been led, sustained, and repeatedly rescued by Black people, Indigenous people, people of color, women, LGBTQ+ people, people with disabilities, immigrants, workers, and countless others whose names never reach a history book. What he draws from each of the three is a lesson in using one’s gifts in service to others: Parton’s Imagination Library, whose Braille Tales partnership with the American Printing House for the Blind fills his own bookshelf with print-and-braille titles his two-year-old granddaughter brings him with the words “Grandpa, read book with your hands!”; Berry’s insistence that community is a daily practice rather than an abstract idea, the conviction behind Adams’s own philosophy of brightening the corner where you are; and Steinem’s advice to young women to listen to themselves rather than to her, together with her understanding that movements require infrastructure and not merely admired personalities.

September 11, 2026 📅️

5.) Unavoidable Bumps – No Shocker And No Shaker | Donna J. Jodhan, LLB, ACSP, MBA | September 11, 2026

Every journey toward meaningful progress has its bumps. Some are unexpected. Others are so deeply embedded in our societies, institutions, and relationships that they are almost impossible to avoid. But what are these unavoidable bumps?

6.) Family Raises $1.6 Million to Build Adaptive Playground | DisabilityScoop.com | September 11, 2026

After five years of fundraising, the Bowling family helped open Berthoud Adaptive Park in Colorado after raising $1.6 million, including more than $50,000 from lemonade stands. Built for 9-year-old Miles Bowling, who uses a wheelchair due to cerebral palsy, the park includes ramps, accessible swings, transfer seating, camera-activated games and an integrated design for children of varied abilities.

7.) Program Aims to Prevent Deadly Police Encounters With People With Disabilities | DisabilityScoop.com | September 11, 2026

Badges and Bridges, a Baltimore-area program led by advocate Mack Dawson and Maryland Department of Transportation Police Sgt. Kevin Moody, brings officers together with people with intellectual, developmental and invisible disabilities before crises occur. Disability Rights Ohio estimates that 30% to 50% of people subjected to police force, and 33% to 50% of those killed, have disabilities.

8.) What It’s Really Like Being A Guide Dog Puppy Raiser | Molly Burke | YouTube.com | September 11, 2026

Conversationally, Molly Burke speaks with a guide dog puppy raiser about the demanding, emotional path of preparing a young dog for its next stage of training. The discussion follows the work from early socialization and daily routines to the difficult handoff, while underscoring the volunteer network behind Guide Dogs of America.

September 10, 2026 📅️

9.) Handi-Link Ministry, Feast, Thrive | Cam Wells | CJAM 99.1 FM | September 10, 2026

This program focuses on disability issues. Host Cam Wells will explore all sides of this comparing and contrasting with able bodied life. This week Featuring: Judy Krasna FEAST, Nicole Frisbie Empowered Abilities and Jeff Tiessen: Thrive.

10.) Rise and Fall | DisabilityDebrief.org | September 10, 2026

Back from an August break, Disability Debrief editor Peter Torres Fremlin examines the rise of the far right in Europe and new research on how the Trump administration’s halt to international aid is affecting disabled people. The edition also covers the rise and fall of a Kenyan advocacy organisation and gathers 119 curated links from 40 countries.

11.) For Blind and Low Vision Voters, Barriers Remain | WomensENews.org | September 10, 2026

Despite HAVA’s requirement that every polling place provide an accessible machine, blind and low-vision voters still report privacy and independence barriers. National Federation of the Blind data found 29.6% of users encountered poll workers unable to activate or set up equipment in 2024, up from 24% in 2020.

12.) Waymo’s Nevada Rollout Violates Accessibility Law, Disability Activist Claims | Streetsblog.org | September 10, 2026

Kelsey Maurine Brickl, a powered-wheelchair user, petitioned Nevada regulators to halt Waymo’s Las Vegas expansion, arguing its newly approved 1,000-vehicle driverless fleet lacks the wheelchair-accessible service state law requires. Waymo said it will comply, but no accessible vehicle meeting its specifications currently exists.

13.) Accessibility Is More Than a Ramp: What Disabled Muslims Need From Our Mosques | Amaliah.com | September 10, 2026

Disabled Muslims face obstacles that extend beyond mosque entrances, from raised thresholds and inaccessible toilets to printed materials unavailable in Braille. Wheelchair user Mohammed Khan and blind NHS psychological therapist Mehrreen Akhtar describe barriers to participation, while Amanati co-founder Zahra Faisal urges accessible infrastructure, disability awareness and disabled people in event planning.

14.) Know a Theatre: Arizona Theatre Matters | AmericanTheatre.org | September 10, 2026

Arizona Theatre Matters founder Jeanmarie Simpson says the company designs digital productions around accessibility from inception, using Blind voice actors, Deaf Artistic Sign Language performers, captions, and audio description. The free, on-demand platform reaches viewers in 194 countries, offers captions in more than 300 languages, and reports 120,000 subscribers and 2.5 million views since the pandemic.

15.) For Musician Tracy Marie, Accessibility Means More Than Getting Through the Door | Ideastream.org | September 10, 2026

Lakewood singer-songwriter Tracy Marie, who has Morquio A syndrome, is pushing Northeast Ohio venues and cities to treat accessibility as an end-to-end requirement, from parking and rest spaces to usable bathrooms and clear paths. An ambulatory wheelchair user, she is helping Lakewood develop an ADA transition plan and advising a University of Illinois accessibility-toolkit project.

16.) For People With Disabilities, Latest DOJ Move Is ‘Another Brick in a Wall’ | McKnightsHomeCare.com | September 10, 2026

On Aug. 31, the DOJ joined Texas, Florida and Alaska in seeking to vacate community-integration provisions in HHS’s 2024 Section 504 rule. Easterseals CEO Kendra Davenport and National Alliance for Care at Home policy VP Damon Terzaghi warned that weaker federal enforcement could expand HCBS waitlists and limit independent living options.

17.) Beyond the Visible-Invisible Disability Binary | PsychologyToday.com | September 10, 2026

Psychologist Kathleen R. Bogart and colleagues Marine Granjon and Pauline Rasset propose a disability observability spectrum, replacing the visible/invisible binary with a context-dependent account of how disability is perceived. More observable disabilities can trigger pity and unwanted help, while less observable ones invite suspicion and “faking it” accusations.

18.) In Cambodia, Accessibility Gap Leaves People With Disabilities Dependent on Others | Cambodianess.com | September 10, 2026

Despite Cambodia’s 2018 technical standards for accessible infrastructure, wheelchair users and blind residents report blocked access to hotels, hospitals, bathrooms, schools and buses. DYNO director Ngin Saorath says monitoring is incomplete; the Social Affairs Ministry acknowledges many facilities are not fully compliant.

19.) Elon Musk’s Blindness Cure Has A Massive Catch… | Legally Blind No Limits | YouTube.com | September 10, 2026

Cutting through the hype around Neuralink’s BlindSight, Cory examines what the proposed vision-restoration implant could actually offer and why its promise comes with serious tradeoffs. The discussion weighs the FDA Breakthrough Device Designation against the invasive S2 implant procedure and the gap between early-stage technology and practical treatment.

20.) Darren Prince: From Addiction To Representing Legends Like Magic Johnson & Muhammad Ali | Sean Callagy | YouTube.com | September 10, 2026

Sitting down with Darren Prince, Sean Callagy examines how recovery, grief, faith, and service have shaped the celebrity agent’s path from addiction to representing figures including Magic Johnson and Muhammad Ali. Their conversation connects personal resilience to sustainable giving, arguing that lasting influence depends on boundaries, authentic relationships, and leaving others better than they were found.

September 9, 2026 📅️

21.) Does Your Employer Discriminate? It’s About to Get Harder to Find Out. | 19thNews.org | September 9, 2026

The EEOC’s Republican majority has voted to end annual EEO-1 workforce demographic reporting, a 60-year practice that helps investigators spot systemic discrimination. The proposed rule, backed by a Project 2025 recommendation, could be finalized by month’s end, leaving employers to retain data but limiting industry comparisons and broader probes.

22.) NCC Pledges Accessible Technology, Digital Skills for Persons With Disabilities | RealNewsMagazine.net | September 9, 2026

Nigeria’s NCC says it will deepen accessible technology and digital-skills programs for persons with disabilities, citing inaccessible products, device and connectivity costs, and weak participation in technology design as barriers. EVC Dr Aminu Maida pointed to assistive ICT tools, an accessible walking-stick prototype and the “Technology Without Barriers” hackathon.

23.) Crip Trip TV Duo Praise North’s Honesty About Accessibility in N.W.T. Visit | CBC.ca | September 9, 2026

Crip Trip’s Danny Ennett and Frederick Kroetsch are filming the show’s third and final season in the Beaufort Delta, travelling through Inuvik to Tuktoyaktuk and the Arctic Ocean. The duo praised the Northwest Territories’ candour about accessibility limits, saying accurate details let them plan around barriers.

24.) Accessibility Shortfalls Keep Bruce County Student Home on First Day of School | CTVNews.ca | September 9, 2026

Quinn Clancy, a 10-year-old with cerebral palsy who uses a walker, stayed home on the first day of school after Walkerton District Community School moved his Grade 5 class to the second floor without a written safety plan. His parents want to know how he will leave the building if the elevator fails; the Bluewater District School Board has invited the family to meet.

25.) Gov’t Reviewing Policy for Stipends, Assistive Devices for Disabled Students – SLTF CEO | MyJoyOnline.com | September 9, 2026

Government is reviewing policy options for stipends and assistive learning devices for tertiary students with disabilities, SLTF CEO Dr Saajida Shiraz said. The Students Loan Trust Fund has spent GH¢10 million on tuition and residential payments for students with disabilities, she said.

26.) Special Education Head at Education Department Abruptly Resigns | NPR.org | September 9, 2026

Kelly Rogers, acting head of the Education Department’s Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services, resigned effective Sept. 11 after less than four months. Kirsten Baesler will take over Sept. 14 as OSERS staff move to HHS; the office administers roughly $15 billion for students with disabilities.

27.) Texas Is Changing How It Funds Special Education. Will Your Child Be Affected? | StarTelegram.com | September 9, 2026

Texas has replaced its special education funding model with eight tiers based on IEP-documented support needs across five areas, rather than where students receive services. The Texas Education Agency says districts are guaranteed at least their old-system funding in 2026-27, while statewide funding is expected to rise by about $250 million.

28.) Autism Dating Series Wins Emmy for Best Reality Show | DisabilityScoop.com | September 9, 2026

Netflix’s Love on the Spectrum won three Creative Arts Emmy Awards, including Outstanding Unstructured Reality Program, for its fourth season. The U.S. autism dating series also earned awards for casting and picture editing, bringing its total across previous seasons to 10; Netflix has renewed it for a fifth season.

29.) Suicide Prevention Month… Tosha Snyder’s Tasty Instant Pot Carbonara… | Cooking Without Looking | YouTube.com | September 9, 2026

In a candid episode, Tosha Snyder shares her journey from vision loss and suicidal crisis to supporting others on a suicide hotline. She also spotlights the importance of contacting 988 during moments of risk, while offering an Instant Pot carbonara recipe as she continues training in vision rehabilitation.

30.) Did Having Kids Ruin The Romance? | Jessica Kellgren-Fozard | YouTube.com | September 9, 2026

Conversationally, Jessica Kellgren-Fozard unpacks how parenthood can reshape intimacy, conflict, and the everyday rhythms of a relationship. The discussion moves from feeling like co-workers after children to recurring arguments, waning romance, and the relationship advice worth leaving behind.

September 8, 2026 📅️

31.) ‘Calm Space’ Installed at Busy West London Tube Station | BBC.com | September 8, 2026

Transport for London is trialling a low-stimulation “calm space” at Ealing Broadway, with an acoustic shelter, seating and nature imagery for passengers who find travel overwhelming. Created with autism charity Autistica, the accessible shelter is designed for mobility aids, pushchairs and assistance dogs; a second trial is planned at the London Transport Museum this autumn.

32.) HHS Office for Civil Rights Reaches Agreement with Pennsylvania Hospital Over Care of Deaf Patient in Emergency Department | HHS.gov | September 8, 2026

HHS OCR reached a resolution agreement with UPMC Williamsport after investigating a complaint that a deaf Emergency Department patient who uses ASL received neither an interpreter nor another aid. The Pennsylvania hospital must revise policies, train personnel, report grievances, and submit six-month compliance reports during two years of OCR monitoring.

33.) Adidas Apologises: Why Did Its Accessibility Campaign Featuring Ex-Israeli Soldier Spark Outrage? | NDTVProfit.com | September 8, 2026

Adidas apologised after an Israel-only campaign for its Single Shoe service featured Shalev Biton, a former Israeli army soldier who lost his left leg in a 2021 Gaza-border attack. Pro-Palestinian activists called for a boycott, saying the ads overlooked Palestinian amputees; the World Health Organisation estimates more than 5,000 limb amputations in Gaza since October 2023.

34.) More Accessible Nightlife Spaces in Halifax Are Needed, Says Local DJ | SaltWire.com | September 8, 2026

Dartmouth DJ and organizer Jessica Hopkinson, who performs as lilboofs, says Halifax bars and event venues routinely block wheelchair users through inaccessible entrances and washrooms, limiting both audiences and bookings. She points to Radstorm as a fully accessible venue as Nova Scotia works toward its 2030 accessibility goal.

35.) For Accessibility, the ADA Set the Foundation. Here’s How Cities Can Aim Higher. | SmartCitiesDive.com | September 8, 2026

Jessica Aiello, founder and CEO of TCS Interpreting, says cities should treat deaf and hard-of-hearing access as a planning priority rather than an ADA compliance exercise. She calls for standard ASL interpretation and real-time captioning at public events, accessibility audits, and ongoing DHH advisory input, especially for emergency communications.

36.) How Federal Immigration Policy Changes Could Threaten Older and Disabled People’s Access to Direct Care | Urban.org | September 8, 2026

Urban Institute’s analysis of 2024 ACS data finds just 35 direct care workers per 1,000 older or disabled US residents, while immigrants account for 28 percent of the workforce. It says the June 2026 Supreme Court decision allowing termination of TPS for 1.3 million Haitian and Syrian immigrants could deepen shortages, particularly in Nevada and Hawaii.

37.) Apple Movie About Disability Rights Activist To Premiere | DisabilityScoop.com | September 8, 2026

Apple Original Films will premiere “Being Heumann” at the Toronto International Film Festival before a Nov. 6 limited theatrical release and Nov. 13 Apple TV debut. Ruth Madeley, who has spina bifida, plays disability-rights leader Judy Heumann, focusing on the 1977 San Francisco Section 504 sit-in that lasted nearly a month.

38.) Neurodivergent Kids Face Special Mental Health Risks. New Initiative Seeks Ways to Protect Them | DisabilityScoop.com | September 8, 2026

Jake Collective and the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention have launched a five-year, $5 million initiative to improve suicide-prevention evidence for neurodivergent children and adolescents. The effort will synthesize existing research, fund studies and develop education for parents and teachers, addressing major gaps in care for autistic youth and those with ADHD.

39.) State Challenged Over Strict IQ Cutoff for IDD Services | DisabilityScoop.com | September 8, 2026

Four Connecticut residents sued the state Department of Developmental Services, alleging its strict IQ cutoff unlawfully denies IDD services to people diagnosed by clinicians whose testing includes a score above 70. The suit says Connecticut is one of three states relying exclusively on such a cutoff and seeks relief that could let hundreds or thousands reapply.

40.) Trump Administration Wants to Strike Rules on Community Integration for People With Disabilities | DisabilityScoop.com | September 8, 2026

The Justice Department and Texas, Alaska, Florida, Louisiana and Montana asked a federal court to vacate Section 504 regulations requiring services in the “most integrated setting.” The proposed resolution in Texas v. Kennedy follows a June DOJ memo rejecting that interpretation; advocates say it weakens enforcement but cannot alter the ADA, Section 504 or Olmstead precedent.

41.) Olena Zelenska Took Part in Third National Forum "My Accessibility – 2026" | President.gov.ua | September 8, 2026

First Lady Olena Zelenska joined more than 350 participants from government, business, municipalities and the veteran community at Ukraine’s third national My Accessibility forum, themed “Lessons Learned.” She cited barrier-free driving schools, nearly 30 ministry accessibility projects and a new State Standard, “Barrier-Free Terminology,” whose vocabulary is now required in official communications.

42.) We Are Pregnant! | Squirmy and Grubs | YouTube.com | September 8, 2026

Announcing their pregnancy, Shane and Hannah Burcaw share the news of a major new chapter for their family. The pair also partners with Babylist to help expecting families by purchasing items from selected registries shared by their community.

September 7, 2026 📅️

43.) Toronto Accessibility Influencer on Her Role in TIFF Opener Being Heumann | CBC.ca | September 7, 2026

Toronto accessibility advocate Taylor Lindsay-Noel, known online as Access by Tay, has a non-speaking role in Being Heumann, Sian Heder’s TIFF opening film about U.S. activist Judith Heumann. Lindsay-Noel says her restaurant and business reviews press venues to publish accurate accessibility information and address barriers such as washrooms and entrances.

44.) Seven in Ten Employers Falling Short on Disability and Neurodiversity Training | HRGrapevine.com | September 7, 2026

A VinciWorks poll found 71% of UK employers have failed to train managers on disability discrimination or staff on neurodiversity; 35% have trained neither group. The survey also found 43% have not updated whistleblowing policies or training since 6 April 2026, when sexual-harassment disclosures became protected whistleblowing disclosures.

45.) Savannah Disability Advocate Urges Georgia Lawmakers to Protect Voting Access As State Weighs New Election System | WTOC.com | September 7, 2026

Georgia’s Joint Election Equipment Specifications and Standards Committee is preparing a recommendation due Jan. 31, 2027, after lawmakers made hand-marked paper ballots the likely default for 2028. Savannah advocate Jessica Mathis urged it to retain accessible ballot-marking devices, citing independent and confidential voting.

46.) Gary O’Donoghue On Journalism, Blindness, And A Career At The BBC | The Global Disability News Network | YouTube.com | September 7, 2026

Sitting down with Gary O’Donoghue, Karina Sturm and Amy Zayed examine his path through British broadcast news and his long-running reporting work in the United States. The conversation covers adapting from analog newsroom tools to screen readers and AI, the visual language of television, and why listening can be a reporting strength.

47.) This Inventor Could Change Air Travel For Wheelchair Users | Driven by Purpose | YouTube.com | September 7, 2026

Sitting down with Dr. Rory Cooper, Driven by Purpose hosts Isaac, Evan, and Mike examine his work to make flying safer and less punishing for power wheelchair users. Cooper outlines designs intended to reduce harmful transfers and wheelchair damage, while making the business case for airlines to serve a major overlooked travel market.

48.) Make Disability Inclusion a Daily Reality | TheDailyStar.net | September 7, 2026

A Tk 1.61-crore school and hostel for 10 visually impaired girls in Kishoreganj has remained unused since its 2019 completion, with officials citing a manpower shortage. The Daily Star notes that the NSPD 2021 found roughly 60% of children with disabilities were outside education, and calls for five staff posts, enrollment, and a nationwide facilities audit.

Last Week 📅️

49.) Roll Out the Ramps: Wheelchair Users Get Accessibility Upgrades in the Glebe | OttawaCitizen.com | September 5, 2026

With the 2026 World Wheelchair Basketball Championships bringing 336 athletes to Ottawa from Sept. 9 to 19, the Glebe BIA is supplying free portable ramps to businesses on Bank Street. Its audit of roughly 300 businesses found almost 40 already met accessibility criteria; about 20 were expected to have ramps available by the tournament’s start.

50.) Alexandra Adams Becomes UK's First Blind and Deaf Doctor Despite the Odds | HypeFresh.com | September 5, 2026

Alexandra Adams, who is deafblind, graduated from Cardiff University Medical School in 2026 and is described as the UK’s first blind and deaf doctor. She uses a Bluetooth stethoscope that streams to her hearing aids, plus phone-based magnification, text-to-speech, and an ophthalmoscope attachment as she prepares to begin work at a Dorset hospital.

51.) Deputy Minister Shares Blind Cricket Experience, Calls for Greater Inclusion | Newswire.lk | September 5, 2026

Deputy Minister Chathuranga Abeysinghe joined the Sri Lanka Council for the Blind’s “Beyond Boundaries” event in Kotte, saying blind cricket demonstrates how sport can remove barriers for people with disabilities. He described its audible plastic ball and steel wickets, underarm bowling, and B1-B3 player classifications.

52.) Interview: David Grabias on "Brailled It" | MoveableFest.com | September 5, 2026

David Grabias’ documentary “Brailled It” hands cameras to nine blind competitors at Los Angeles’ Braille Challenge, using participant-shot footage to create an audio-first experience. Grabias and editor Edgar Sardarian narrowed the film to Chris, Salome, and Isaiah, incorporating family feedback, audio description, and 3D spatial sound.

53.) The Blogs: I Don’t Ask What Their Disability Is. I Ask What They Need to Succeed | TimesOfIsrael.com | September 4, 2026

Krembo Wings CEO Liat Ellert says Israel’s inclusive youth movement serves about 8,000 children and teens with and without disabilities across 85 branches, while more than 500 children remain on waiting lists. Funding gaps threaten existing branches as municipalities request new locations.

54.) Disability Task Force Recommends Accessible Rideshares, Events, Removing Pathway Barriers, and More | BoiseDev.com | September 4, 2026

Boise’s Cross Disability Task Force asked City Council to pursue accessible on-demand rides, safer pedestrian routes, event audits, and a formalized task force. The volunteers want at least one wheelchair-accessible rideshare vehicle operating by 2027; Boise has not yet opened talks with providers.

55.) I’m on the Spectrum – and So Are You! Definition of Autism So Broad That It’s Meaningless | NYPost.com | September 4, 2026

Family physician Leonard Sax argues that a European study found autism diagnoses without intellectual disability rose 1,800% from 2001 to 2020, while diagnoses involving intellectual disability remained flat. He cites University College London professor Uta Frith’s warning that diagnostic inflation can pathologize normal variation and points to misleading autism content on TikTok.

56.) 60 Years of Disability Progress Helped My Brother. I Fear We’re Reversing It | KansasCity.com | September 4, 2026

Gary Blumenthal, a former Kansas legislator and federal disability official, warns that Trump administration Medicaid cuts and January 2027 work and reporting requirements could weaken home- and community-based services for people with disabilities. He cites his brother Steve’s path from institutionalization to a Medicaid-funded group home in Lawrence.

57.) My Disability Wasn’t the Problem. The Assumptions About It Were. | PublicSource.org | September 4, 2026

After seeking an ADA accommodation for transplant-related testing and symptoms, cybersecurity specialist Zarin Hamid says she was put on a performance improvement plan a week after approval and fired 60 days later. The Pittsburgh-based advocate later returned to cybersecurity, using her experience to challenge workplace assumptions about disabled workers.

58.) ‘A Real Kick in the Teeth’: Dozens of Tram Stops Have Been Upgraded, but Wheelchair Users Still Can’t Board | TheAge.com | September 4, 2026

Melbourne’s route 57 and 59 works for 25-metre G-class trams have merged or moved 15 stops without adding level-access platforms. Just 29 per cent of stops across the network are level-access, despite Victoria missing its 2022 accessibility deadline; advocate Andrew Bretherton calls the gap a form of segregation.

59.) A Remarkable Documentary Made by Blind Students: ‘We Were Stunned by the Footage’ | TheGuardian.com | September 4, 2026

Brailled It follows the 2024 Braille Challenge at the University of Southern California, where more than 1,100 blind and visually impaired students competed. Director David Grabias gave cameras to three competitors – Salome Cummins, Christopher Morgan and Isaiah Gauthier – who are credited as co-directors.

60.) Blind Center of Nevada Opens Visions Park | ReviewJournal.com | September 4, 2026

Blind Center of Nevada opened Visions Park, a $40 million, 99-unit affordable housing community for blind or visually impaired Southern Nevadans. The ADA-accessible development includes audio-tactile walkways and optional services including an AI Innovation Lab, mobility training, workforce development, and mental health navigation.

61.) Smart Glasses Helped a Man See the World. The Privacy Panic Took It Away | San.com | September 4, 2026

About: National Organization on Disability is a nonprofit that works with large employers to increase the hiring, retention and advancement of people with disabilities. It was founded in 1982, growing out of the United Nations International Year of Disabled Persons, by Alan A. Reich, the first person to address the UN General Assembly from a wheelchair. In the four decades since, it has moved from broad public-awareness work toward a business-to-business focus, presenting disability inclusion as a question of business performance rather than charity. That posture is captured in the organization’s own line, “Unlocking human potential. Enhancing business performance.” Headquartered in Washington, D.C. and led by President and Chief Executive Officer Beth Sirull, National Organization on Disability earns most of its support from the employers it serves rather than from individual donors.

Its employer work runs on four connected programs. The Leadership Council is a paid corporate membership network, currently listing 35 member organizations, offering access to disability-inclusion specialists, talent-acquisition support, peer networking and public recognition. The Disability Inclusion Blueprint is a free, confidential self-assessment that benchmarks an employer across talent outcomes, strategy and policies, and practices and programs; top-quartile participants who opt in earn the Leading Disability Employer Seal. EnAble Learning is an on-demand training platform whose self-paced courses cover disability fundamentals, neurodiversity at work, managing teams through rising mental-health challenges, and accessibility in artificial intelligence and emerging technology. A Speakers Bureau books disability advocates, athletes, creators and staff for corporate events and employee resource group meetings. Alongside these, National Organization on Disability conducts federal policy advocacy and research, the latter increasingly through a federally funded university consortium studying disability employment policy.

About: The Inspiration Foundation is a 501(c)(3) public charity working to increase the employment rate of people with disabilities. It was founded in 2006 by Isaac Shapiro and Mike Ghesser, the co-founders of the bath and body care brand Cleanlogic, and named for Isaac’s mother, Beatriz “Bea” Shapiro, who lost her sight to retinitis pigmentosa at about seven years old. Bea went on to become a long-distance runner, to found a technology training center for blind and visually impaired people, and to work as a vocational rehabilitation counselor for the State of Arizona. Her frustration was a practical one: the assistive technology disabled jobseekers were being trained on was too often out of date before they ever reached an interview. For its first two decades the Foundation answered that directly, awarding grants to nonprofit organizations serving blind and low-vision people so they could put current screen readers and Braille displays in front of the people who need them, including a dedicated fund for VisionServe Alliance member organizations.

In 2026 the Foundation appointed Jeremy Grandstaff as its first Executive Director. Grandstaff is blind, holds degrees in management information systems and organization development from Bowling Green State University, and brings two decades of organizational development and change management experience to the role. Under his leadership the Foundation has set a goal of increasing employment for people with disabilities by ten percent over the next five years, pursued through two pipelines running at once: a stronger pipeline of candidates, supported by the technology grant program, and a pipeline of employers who are actively hiring, promoting and retaining people with disabilities. The employer side of that work is being formalized into a certification called the Inspiration Seal, currently in pilot while its criteria are developed. Organizations interested in the technology grant program can reach Jeremy Grandstaff directly at jgrandstaff@inspirationfoundation.org.

Subscribe here. Review the most recent issues here. Access Information refers to informational topics that directly affect the lives of people with disabilities. Access Information includes any and all information related to bettering the lives of people who are blind, low vision, deaf, hard of hearing, deafblind, neurodivergent and/or disabled. Access Information News is a Mind Vault Solutions, Ltd. Publication. Publisher: Aaron Di Blasi. Editors: John Hanlin, Jenna Lang and Vicki Walton. item.content:encoded:
♿️ The Week’s News in Access Information

Access Information News. The world’s #1 online resource for current news and trends in access information.

A Mind Vault Solutions, Ltd. Publication

Subscribers:  47,625 🔢️ opt-in subscribers were sent this issue via email.

Social Media:  199,512 🔢️ readers were sent this issue via social media, courtesy of the PWD Media Distribution Co-Op.

Share: Facebook | X (Twitter) | LinkedIn | Email | Web Link | How to read this newsletter if you are blind or low-vision.

Section Jumper: Sponsors | Access Awareness | Featured Advertisement | News | Featured Events | Classified Ads | Supporters | News Team | Subscription Information

Sponsors 🏅️

Access Awareness: Updates That Matter ♿️

Things I Don’t Buy As A Montessori Parent (Save Your Money) | Jessica Kellgren-Fozard | YouTube.com | September 2, 2026

Cutting through the hype around Montessori shopping, Jessica Kellgren-Fozard examines which pricey toddler products she skips and why everyday routines can better support independence. She also outlines the practical non-Montessori purchases she wishes had entered family life sooner, separating useful conveniences from costly clutter.

This Week’s Featured Advertisement ️

Sponsorship Packages Currently Available: Join Industry Leaders in Supporting Free Access Information News For Disabled Readers All Over The World While Increasing Traffic To Your Properties Each Week. Advertise in every issue. Or just one.

Join Access Information News as a Sponsor today and begin reaching over 47,000 access information readers each week, all while supporting the ongoing distribution of Access Information News for those very same readers. Only $200 / month.

Key Newsletter Statistics:

  • Subscribers: 47,000 + per week and growing.
  • Open Rate: 47% (Average. Last 12 months.)
  • Click Rate: 34% (Average. Last 12 months.)
  • Bounce Rate: 1.2% (Average. Last 12 months.)
  • Ad CTRs: 2-12% (Average. Last 12 months.)

Benefits All Sponsors Receive:

  • One (1) Sponsor Profile on the Access Information News website, for the duration of your sponsorship.
  • One (1) Sponsor Profile in each weekly newsletter, for the duration of your sponsorship.
  • One (1) Sponsor Wall Brand Advertisement on the Access Information News home page + every page of the website (Right Side Bar: Sponsors), for the duration of your sponsorship.
  • One (1) Sponsor Wall Brand Advertisement in each weekly newsletter, for the duration of your sponsorship.
  • One (1) Classified Advertisement in each weekly newsletter, for the duration of your sponsorship.
  • Membership in the PWD Media Co-Op, for the duration of your sponsorship.
  • 50% Discount on all Sponsored News Article Advertisements, for the duration of your sponsorship.
  • Free link tracking, for all time.
  • Permanent SEO benefits. (All Sponsor Profiles are archived on the Access Information News website at the close of Sponsorship. Driving traffic back to your properties for all time.
  • Gratitude from over 47,000 blind, low vision, deaf, hard of hearing, deafblind, neurodivergent and/or disabled professionals, educators, and enthusiasts, all over the world, along with the caregivers, companies and organizations that serve and support them, for keeping Access Information News free to read each week.

With additional benefits for Sponsors who choose to pay quarterly or annually. Learn more about Sponsorship today. today.

News 📰️

👉 Submit a news article for free here, with timing and placement determined by our editors.

👉 Submit a Sponsored News Article here, with timing and placement determined by you.

1.) Top 5 Most Clicked News Articles From Last Week 📊️

A.) I Blindfolded My Fiancé For 24 Hours | Molly Burke | YouTube.com | August 25, 2026

For a 24-hour empathy experiment, Molly Burke blindfolds her fiance and documents how he navigates a day without sight. The challenge puts everyday routines at the center of a conversation about accessibility, independence, and the assumptions sighted people can bring to daily life.

B.) I’m Not The Dad I Thought I’d Be… | Legally Blind No Limits | YouTube.com | August 26, 2026

Navigating a hectic school drop-off, Legally Blind No Limits recounts the first day at a new school with his seven-year-old son as a legally blind parent. With his white cane and mobility training guiding the route, the experience becomes an unexpected reflection on his son’s growing instinct to help lead the way.

C.) Access Information News Welcomes Jeremy Grandstaff and The Inspiration Foundation | Aaron Di Blasi, Publisher | August 31, 2026

Please join me in giving a warm welcome to Jeremy Grandstaff and The Inspiration Foundation, who has so very graciously agreed to support the ongoing distribution of Access Information News via sponsorship. If you enjoy reading Access Information News for free each week, it is Sponsors like Jeremy Grandstaff and The Inspiration Foundation that make it possible. And as I always say, these are the people, businesses and organizations that deserve your attention. Because they are the ones paying attention to the needs of the disability community.

The Inspiration Foundation is a 501(c)(3) public nonprofit working to increase the employment rate of people with disabilities. It was founded in 2006 by Isaac Shapiro and Mike Ghesser, the co-founders of the bath and body care brand Cleanlogic, and named for Isaac’s mother, Beatriz “Bea” Shapiro, who lost her sight to retinitis pigmentosa at about seven years old. Bea went on to become a long-distance runner, to found a technology training center for blind and visually impaired people, and to work as an assistive technology specialist for the State of Arizona. Her frustration was a practical one: the assistive technology disabled jobseekers were being trained on was too often out of date before they ever reached an interview. For its first two decades the Foundation answered that directly, awarding grants to nonprofit organizations serving blind and low-vision people so they could put current screen readers and Braille displays in front of the people who need them, including a dedicated fund for VisionServe Alliance member organizations.

In 2026 the Foundation appointed Jeremy Grandstaff as its first Executive Director. Grandstaff is blind, holds degrees in management information systems and organization development from Bowling Green State University, and brings two decades of organizational development and change management experience to the role. Under his leadership the Foundation has set a goal of increasing employment for people with disabilities by ten percent over the next five years, pursued through two pipelines running at once: a stronger pipeline of candidates, supported by the technology grant program, and a pipeline of employers who are actively hiring, promoting and retaining people with disabilities. The employer side of that work is being formalized into a certification called the Inspiration Seal, currently in pilot while its criteria are developed. Organizations interested in the technology grant program can reach Jeremy Grandstaff directly at jgrandstaff@inspirationfoundation.org 📧️.

D.) Guardians Are Supposed to Care for Our Most Vulnerable. Why Are Exploitation Cases Skyrocketing? | DisabilityScoop.com | August 27, 2026

New Jersey’s Guardianship Monitoring Program reported 694 escalated concerns to judges in 2025, up from 252 in 2024, including nearly 90 cases involving inappropriate, un-itemized or unexplained disbursements. The state has more than 37,000 guardianships overseeing $1.2 billion in reported assets.

E.) Federal Appeals Court Sides With Lyft in Wheelchair Accessibility Lawsuit | WestchesterNews12.com | August 27, 2026

A federal appeals court ruled Lyft is not required to provide wheelchair-accessible vehicles nationwide, affirming a lower-court win for the ride-hailing company. Westchester Disabled on the Move alleged limits on vehicles for fixed-frame wheelchairs violated the Americans with Disabilities Act and New York Human Rights Law; the court found its proposed remedies would not deliver effective accessible transportation.

September 7, 2026 📅️

2.) The Innovative Impact Newsletter By Dr. Kirk Adams for Monday, September 7, 2026 – Issue 118 | Dr. Kirk Adams | September 7, 2026

The Innovative Impact Newsletter By Dr. Kirk Adams is the world’s leading business strategy and workplace inclusion newsletter that reaches over 6,000 corporate executives, HR professionals, policymakers, disability advocates, and business leaders all over the world, each month.

3.) The Doors Are Open: How to Join the Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion | Dr. Kirk Adams, Executive Director, ISDI | September 7, 2026

Here, Dr. Kirk Adams announces that the Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion went live on September 1, 2026, opened not with a webinar or a panel but with an “Ask Us Anything” hour of questions, frustrations, ideas and lived experience. He explains what the Coalition actually is: a way for members to move from reactive, isolated survival mode to strategic, sustainable, collective power, built on four words, Connect, Learn, Act, Together. He is direct about who it is for, which is everybody, and equally direct that disability inclusion and accessibility are not a side room in it but a dedicated space by design. Inside, he describes three things above all others: BELONG, the peer circles where saying “I am overwhelmed” is met with practical help rather than judgment; CLARITY, a trusted translation layer of plain-language briefings and expert-guided sessions; and POWER, the shared tools, cross-sector strategy and coalition-backed influence that turn isolated effort into coordinated action. In practice that means Ask the Experts office hours, a Member Lounge and Directory, a growing Resource Library, a Rapid Response Hub for the moments that will not wait, legislative and legal updates, podcasts featuring DEIAB voices, and a shared calendar of events worth your time.

4.) Recording: Official Launch of The Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion | Dr. Kirk Adams, Executive Director, ISDI | September 7, 2026

Here, Dr. Kirk Adams shares the full recording of the September 1, 2026 public launch of the Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion, the national membership community created by the Institute for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion to help people working in diversity, equity, inclusion, accessibility and belonging move from reactive, isolated survival mode to strategic, sustainable, collective power.

September 4, 2026 📅️

5.) BMG Blind Money Gang: Vegas Trip Studio Session Behind The Scenes | Even Though I’m Blind | YouTube.com | September 4, 2026

Showcasing BMG Blind Money Gang’s Vegas trip and studio session, Even Though I’m Blind documents behind-the-scenes moments from the group’s time in Las Vegas. The footage pairs travel-day context with a look at the studio work, placing the creative process alongside the trip.

6.) What It’s Really Like Building A DIY Empire Online From Your College Dorm | Molly Burke | YouTube.com | September 4, 2026

Sitting down with LaurDIY, Molly Burke traces Lauren Riihimaki’s path from a creatively encouraged childhood in Canada to building an enduring online DIY business. Their conversation covers thrifted dorm decor, early YouTube collaborations, difficult contracts, creator burnout, and the shift from content creation into product design and business ownership.

7.) Watching TV with Vision Loss: What Can Help | HadleyHelps.org | September 4, 2026

Hadley practical help specialist Steve Kelly recommends adjusting seating and glare before buying specialized TV aids, warning that oversize screens can force uncomfortable head movement. He and host Ricky Enger also point to accessible cable boxes, Apple TV, Amazon Fire TV Stick, universal remotes, and audio description as ways to make viewing easier after vision loss. On Spotify. On Apple Podcasts.

8.) Daily Accessibility Challenges of Persons With Disability (PWDs) | CebuDailyNews.inquirer.net | September 4, 2026

Four decades after the Philippines enacted Batas Pambansa Blg. 344, wheelchair users still face steep ramps, broken sidewalks, poorly designed elevators, and inaccessible transport. Mae Chan Li’s 10-minute Cinemalaya documentary “Para-Paraan” follows para powerlifter Katrina Hernandez through routine errands that expose those systemic barriers.

9.) How Can We Instill More Teamwork | Donna J. Jodhan, LLB, ACSP, MBA | BarrierFreeCanada.org | September 4, 2026

We seem to have either forgotten the meaning of the word teamwork, or perhaps we have simply lost sight of what teamwork truly means.

September 3, 2026 📅️

10.) Watch This Short Video To Discover Excellent Reasons To Subscribe To The Blind Kitchen Newsletter! | The Blind Kitchen | YouTube.com | September 3, 2026

Showcasing its newsletter, The Blind Kitchen outlines why the publication is central to its ongoing outreach and community updates. The brief presentation directs interested subscribers to the organization’s website and contact channel for further details.

11.) IAMAI Flags Overlap Between Draft RPwD Rules and MIB Accessibility Norms | BestMediaInfo.com | September 3, 2026

IAMAI has urged the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment to avoid uniform accessibility mandates under draft RPwD rules, warning they could override MIB’s sector-specific framework. The group wants phased requirements, with feasibility, cost and technology assessments for platforms, software and hardware.

12.) Lawmakers Consider How to Protect Voting Access for People With Disabilities, Non-English Speakers | GeorgiaRecorder.com | September 3, 2026

Georgia lawmakers preparing to move to hand-marked paper ballots by 2028 are being pressed to retain ballot-marking devices with audio and large-print formats. Asian Americans Advancing Justice-Atlanta’s Anar Parik said the next system should add languages through software rather than require replacement equipment as language-access requirements evolve.

13.) Blind Music Therapist Helps Those With Disabilities Find Their Voice in Santa Barbara | Keyt.com | September 3, 2026

Meghan Downing, a legally blind music therapist at Santa Barbara’s ArtLabbé Academy, leads weekly sessions for people with developmental disabilities, drawing on her experience with Stargardt disease. Founder Nathaniel Grotenhuis says the organization has grown to more than 140 weekly participants across 12 classrooms and organizations in under a year.

14.) Film Industry Responds to Supreme Court Ruling on Accessibility: ‘Agree on Expanding Convenience, but Government Support Needed’ | SBS.co.kr | September 3, 2026

South Korea’s Supreme Court ruled that limiting accessibility services to 3% of screenings at theaters with 300 or more seats improperly prioritized operators’ financial burden, sending a disability-discrimination case back to the Seoul High Court. CGV, Lotte Cinema, and Megabox face potentially broader duties to provide audio descriptions, subtitles, and receiving devices, while calling for government support and industry-wide standards.

15.) Supreme Court Orders Cinemas to Expand Accessibility for Disabled Viewers | Chosun.com | September 3, 2026

According to the report’s title, the Supreme Court has ordered cinemas to expand accessibility for disabled viewers. The supplied text provides no further details on the ruling, the cinema operators involved, or the required accommodations.

16.) How the Stories We Tell Shape Our Perspective of Disability | DisabilityBelongs.org | September 3, 2026

Disability Belongs says portrayals in books, film, television, faith communities, and everyday language can shape assumptions about disabled people. The disability-led nonprofit calls for representation that includes leadership, relationships, work, flaws, and joy, rather than reducing people to pity, charity, diagnosis, or overcoming hardship.

17.) Supreme Court Backs Subtitles, Audio Descriptions for Disabled Audiences | KoreaTimes.co.kr | September 3, 2026

South Korea’s Supreme Court ruled that cinemas’ failure to provide audio descriptions, subtitles and receiving devices for visually and hearing-impaired patrons is disability discrimination. It overturned a 2021 Seoul High Court limit requiring accessibility services for only 3% of screenings at theaters with 300 or more seats, faulting its emphasis on operators’ financial burden.

18.) Pacific Beach School Makes Inclusion Its Mission for Children With Disabilities | NBCSanDiego.com | September 3, 2026

In Pacific Beach, Includ(Ed), founded in 2024, combines child care for children ages 3 months through pre-kindergarten with physical, occupational, speech and music therapy. Executive Director Anna Chiles says the school serves 30 children across two sites, often at a 2-to-1 student-to-adult ratio, while keeping tuition comparable to other day cares through donations, fundraising and scholarships.

19.) Where Is There Progress in Meeting ADA Digital Accessibility Standards and What New Challenges Are Emerging? | NewAmerica.org | September 3, 2026

After the DOJ delayed its ADA Title II digital-accessibility compliance dates by one year on April 20, 2026, New America says public entities still must meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA. The group warns that proposed E-Rate cuts and Medicaid reductions could force school districts to choose between connectivity, assistive technology, and compliance.

September 2, 2026 📅️

20.) Things I Don’t Buy As A Montessori Parent (Save Your Money) | Jessica Kellgren-Fozard | YouTube.com | September 2, 2026

Cutting through the hype around Montessori shopping, Jessica Kellgren-Fozard examines which pricey toddler products she skips and why everyday routines can better support independence. She also outlines the practical non-Montessori purchases she wishes had entered family life sooner, separating useful conveniences from costly clutter.

21.) ADA Web Rule Sends Legislatures Racing Toward Digital Access | NCSL.org | September 2, 2026

Federal rules issued by the DOJ and HHS in 2024 require public digital content to meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA, putting state legislatures on deadlines that extend to 2027 or 2028. At an NCSL summit, Colorado, Minnesota and Wisconsin officials cited inaccessible PDFs, legislative markup and archival records as the hardest problems, with staff training and workflow checks central to compliance.

22.) Visiting Helen Keller’s Birthplace While Deaf: What It Means to Navigate Accessibility | LitHub.com | September 2, 2026

Rachel Kolb recounts visiting Ivy Green, Helen Keller’s Alabama birthplace, in 2018 after staff could not arrange an ASL interpreter. The Deaf writer uses the failed accommodation to trace the post-ADA burden of requesting access, contrasting Keller’s individualist public myth with disability solidarity and the ongoing labor of navigating institutions.

23.) ‘We Need Accessibility’: Sioux Falls Resident Calls for Expanded Paratransit Limits | DakotaNewsNow.com | September 2, 2026

Sioux Falls resident Robert Elliot says the city’s paratransit boundary leaves him unable to pre-book rides to an orthopedic hospital at 69th Street and Louise. Operator Via says ADA rules require service within three-quarters of a mile of fixed routes; the facility is outside that zone, though wheelchair-accessible SAM On-Demand is available.

24.) Advocates Call for Greater Accessibility for Deaf Residents in Montgomery County | NewsChannel5.com | September 2, 2026

Two advocates asked the Montgomery County Commission to improve access to government services and public meetings for deaf residents. Deaf advocate Brice Pruyn and ASL interpreter Artie Terrell Grassman proposed meeting interpreters and officer technology that can connect residents to interpreters; the commission had not acted as of Wednesday.

25.) Blind and Disabled Californians Put on Indefinite Waitlist as DOR Crisis Deepens | Patricia Leetz | September 2, 2026

Californians who are blind, low vision, DeafBlind, or have other disabilities are being denied timely access to the vocational rehabilitation services they need to find work, remain independent, and even keep the jobs they already have. The California Department of Rehabilitation has closed all service categories under an Order of Selection, placing new applicants on an indefinite waitlist with no timeline for help. For someone who needs assistive technology, rehabilitation training, orientation and mobility services, or support to prevent the loss of a job, waiting indefinitely can have devastating and irreversible consequences. A campaign is calling upon California legislators to hold an urgent joint legislative hearing addressing the crisis, emergency funding, and oversight. Californians are encouraged to send the letter and add their own experiences. Every letter helps demonstrate that delay is not harmless and that people’s jobs, independence, and futures are already at risk.

September 1, 2026 📅️

26.) Do I Actually Know What Animals Look Like?? | Molly Burke | YouTube.com | September 1, 2026

Reflecting on how blindness shapes visual understanding, Molly Burke considers what she knows about the appearance of animals. The conversation examines the gap between learned descriptions, touch, sound, and the mental images people form of the natural world.

27.) Finding Connection In “Siren: The Voices Of Shelley Beattie” | The Global Disability News Network | YouTube.com | September 1, 2026

In an analytical review, Rikki Poynter examines how Siren: The Voices of Shelley Beattie portrays the life and legacy of Deaf bodybuilder and actor Shelley “Siren” Beattie. The 103-minute documentary pairs director Irene Taylor with narrator and producer Marlee Matlin, following screenings at DOC NYC and the Deaf Way Film Festival.

28.) Impending Changes to Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act | Nod.org | September 1, 2026

The U.S. Department of Labor’s final Section 503 rule, effective September 21, 2026, eliminates the CC-305 disability self-identification form, the 7% utilization goal, and required disability data collection for applicants, referrals, and hires. Nondiscrimination, affirmative action, reasonable-accommodation, and outreach requirements remain, while the contract coverage threshold rises to $20,000.

29.) State Records Show Abuse and Neglect Continues in New Hampshire’s Disability System in 2026 | NewHampshireBulletin.com | September 1, 2026

New Hampshire state records show 280 abuse, neglect, or exploitation reports in its disability care system from January through June 2026; investigators deemed 75 credible, including 21 abuse cases. The same records list 30 deaths, 12 unanticipated, as the state begins implementing SB 670 oversight reforms.

30.) BlindShell Newsletter September! | MailChimp.mp | September 1, 2026

BlindShell has added the myIKONN app to the BlindShell Classic 2 App Catalog and the BlindShell Classic 3 popular-apps list, enabling spoken measurements from compatible IKONN household devices. The September newsletter also covers WhatsApp, ScriptTalk and Quiz Game updates, plus repair technician Jan’s advice on water damage and battery recovery.

31.) Just Ask: Working Alongside Blind and Low Vision Colleagues | Moosend.com | September 1, 2026

NRTC released Just Ask: Working Alongside Blind and Low Vision Colleagues, a workplace-etiquette video for coworkers, supervisors, HR teams, and organizational leaders. Its companion quick reference covers accessible documents and meetings, workplace orientation, assistive technology, communication, and inclusive participation.

About: National Organization on Disability is a nonprofit that works with large employers to increase the hiring, retention and advancement of people with disabilities. It was founded in 1982, growing out of the United Nations International Year of Disabled Persons, by Alan A. Reich, the first person to address the UN General Assembly from a wheelchair. In the four decades since, it has moved from broad public-awareness work toward a business-to-business focus, presenting disability inclusion as a question of business performance rather than charity. That posture is captured in the organization’s own line, “Unlocking human potential. Enhancing business performance.” Headquartered in Washington, D.C. and led by President and Chief Executive Officer Beth Sirull, National Organization on Disability earns most of its support from the employers it serves rather than from individual donors.

Its employer work runs on four connected programs. The Leadership Council is a paid corporate membership network, currently listing 35 member organizations, offering access to disability-inclusion specialists, talent-acquisition support, peer networking and public recognition. The Disability Inclusion Blueprint is a free, confidential self-assessment that benchmarks an employer across talent outcomes, strategy and policies, and practices and programs; top-quartile participants who opt in earn the Leading Disability Employer Seal. EnAble Learning is an on-demand training platform whose self-paced courses cover disability fundamentals, neurodiversity at work, managing teams through rising mental-health challenges, and accessibility in artificial intelligence and emerging technology. A Speakers Bureau books disability advocates, athletes, creators and staff for corporate events and employee resource group meetings. Alongside these, National Organization on Disability conducts federal policy advocacy and research, the latter increasingly through a federally funded university consortium studying disability employment policy.

About: The Inspiration Foundation is a 501(c)(3) public charity working to increase the employment rate of people with disabilities. It was founded in 2006 by Isaac Shapiro and Mike Ghesser, the co-founders of the bath and body care brand Cleanlogic, and named for Isaac’s mother, Beatriz “Bea” Shapiro, who lost her sight to retinitis pigmentosa at about seven years old. Bea went on to become a long-distance runner, to found a technology training center for blind and visually impaired people, and to work as a vocational rehabilitation counselor for the State of Arizona. Her frustration was a practical one: the assistive technology disabled jobseekers were being trained on was too often out of date before they ever reached an interview. For its first two decades the Foundation answered that directly, awarding grants to nonprofit organizations serving blind and low-vision people so they could put current screen readers and Braille displays in front of the people who need them, including a dedicated fund for VisionServe Alliance member organizations.

In 2026 the Foundation appointed Jeremy Grandstaff as its first Executive Director. Grandstaff is blind, holds degrees in management information systems and organization development from Bowling Green State University, and brings two decades of organizational development and change management experience to the role. Under his leadership the Foundation has set a goal of increasing employment for people with disabilities by ten percent over the next five years, pursued through two pipelines running at once: a stronger pipeline of candidates, supported by the technology grant program, and a pipeline of employers who are actively hiring, promoting and retaining people with disabilities. The employer side of that work is being formalized into a certification called the Inspiration Seal, currently in pilot while its criteria are developed. Organizations interested in the technology grant program can reach Jeremy Grandstaff directly at jgrandstaff@inspirationfoundation.org.

Founded in 2022, Access Information News is the world’s leading not-for-profit access information news publication that reaches over 45,000 blind, low vision, deaf, hard of hearing, deafblind, neurodivergent and/or disabled professionals, educators and enthusiasts, all over the world, each week, along with the caregivers, companies and organizations that serve and support them. Subscribe here. Review the most recent issues here. Access Information refers to informational topics that directly affect the lives of people with disabilities. Access Information includes any and all information related to bettering the lives of people who are blind, low vision, deaf, hard of hearing, deafblind, neurodivergent and/or disabled. Access Information News is a Mind Vault Solutions, Ltd. Publication. Publisher: Aaron Di Blasi. Editors: John Hanlin, Jenna Lang and Vicki Walton. Access Information News is a sponsor, reader and advertiser supported publication.

Either of these methods will provide you with an accessibly friendly and secure medium through which you can subscribe to our mailing list. There are no restrictions placed on these documents. Complete list of all back issues available. Premium Subscribers are entitled to all back issues, anytime they sign up.
